text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Hotels on the Slovenian coast were over 50-percent occupied in the first half of March, partly due to warm weather, and said they expected a very good summer season.

- The United List of Social Democrats, the former communist party, elected Borut Pahor as the new president. Pahor will replace Janez Kocijancic who decided not to run for re-election after the party gained only nine parliamentary seats in a November general election, down from 14 four years ago.
- Due to a lack of snow there is a possibility the final ski-jumping competition of the 1996/97 World Cup in Planica, Slovenia, could be cancelled.
- Most Slovenian electricity producers and distributors oppose a possible merger of all electricity companies in Slovenia that has been proposed by main distributor Eles.
- Drug company Krka plans to open a new factory wing in Novo mesto, that cost $13.5 million, in April.
- Minister of Education Slavko Gaber said the government did not plan to introduce religious education in state schools.

- Although Slovenian ski-jumper Primoz Peterka came 16th in the Sunday World Cup competition in Holmenkollen, he still leads overall and is likely to become the first Slovenian to win the overall World Cup gold.
